result.title: Less from More: Reinforcing Sparse Video Reasoning from Dense References
result.summary: Video-language models commonly assume that more temporal observations lead to more reliable reasoning. We question this assumption and argue that the key challenge is not merely processing more video frames efficiently, but learning to reason reliably under limited temporal evidence. We propose SAVER, a dense-to-sparse post-training framework that uses dense video views as training-time references for sparse-frame inference. During reinforcement post-training, paired dense and sparse views are optimized with grounding rewards and a reliability-gated reference reward, encouraging sparse view predictions to preserve task-relevant temporal evidence. Notably, SAVER is trained only on 1,250 randomly sampled temporal grounding examples, without using any video question answering annotations. Across three temporal grounding benchmarks and six video question-answering benchmarks, SAVER consistently improves performance across frame budgets. In particular, SAVER can match or surpass dense-frame Qwen3.5 baselines while using substantially fewer frames. These results show that temporal grounding can serve as an effective evidence-localization proxy for learning sparse video reasoning that transfers to broader video understanding tasks.

AI.brief_summary: 论文质疑「观测越多推理越可靠」，提出 SAVER 这一 dense-to-sparse 后训练框架：训练时以配对稠密/稀疏视频视角为参照，用 grounding 奖励与可靠性门控的参考奖励进行强化后训练，促使稀疏帧预测保留任务相关时序证据，并在时序定位与视频问答基准上验证少帧即可匹配或超过稠密帧基线。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接对应「视觉证据筛选」与有限证据下推理：时序 grounding 作为证据定位代理这一思路，可供核查训练期稠密参照如何影响稀疏视角保留任务必要信息的机制及其与帧预算、证据充分性决策的联系。
